question: Using the Rust blog post at https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/10/02/demoting-i686-windows-targets-to-std-only/, summarize what is changing for 32-bit Windows targets, from which Rust release, what users must do instead, and why.

facts.claim: Starting with Rust 1.100.0, the i686 Windows targets (i686-pc-windows-msvc and i686-pc-windows-gnu) are demoted to tiers without host tools: the compiler and tools are no longer shipped for them.
facts.evidence: source line 90: "With Rust 1.100.0, the following changes to 32-bit Windows targets will happen:"; source line 92: "Tier 1 with host tools target will be demoted to Tier 1 without host tools."; source line 93: "Tier 2 with host tools target will be demoted to Tier 2 without host tools."

facts.claim: The standard library is still shipped for these targets, so users build 32-bit Windows programs by cross-compiling from a supported host such as 64-bit Windows.
facts.evidence: source line 95: "Builds of the standard library will continue to be distributed, but host tools such as the compiler will be no longer available."; source line 96: "To build 32-bit Windows binaries, cross-compiling from a still-supported host toolchain (such as a 64-bit Windows ones) will be required from now on."

facts.claim: Why: 32-bit Windows is obsolete (no 32-bit-only x86 CPUs sold for over 15 years, Windows 32-bit support ended in October 2025), and building the i686 Windows toolchains has been a source of problems (crashes, out-of-memory failures).
facts.evidence: source line 99: "Desktop and Server 32-bit only x86 CPUs are no longer sold for over 15 years, and general 32-bit Windows support has ended in October 2025."; source line 100: "We have encountered compiler binaries crashing when built with the i686 MSVC target, and the GNU C++ toolchain failing with OOMs during LLVM build."

question: https://toss.tech/article/nic-interrupt-bottleneck 글의 요지를 요약해 주세요. 커밋 지연의 원인은 무엇이었고, 어떻게 해결했으며, 결과는 어땠나요?

facts.claim: Cause: NIC interrupts concentrated on one CPU socket competed for CPU with Oracle's log writer (LGWR), delaying redo-log writes and therefore commits.
facts.evidence: source line 282: "원인은 CPU 소켓 하나에 몰려 있던 NIC 인터럽트였습니다"; source line 282: "NIC 인터럽트가 물리 코어 32개 중 8개에만 몰려 있었습니다"

facts.claim: Fix: the interconnect NICs were moved to slots on different CPU sockets and their bonding switched to Active-Active, spreading the interrupts across both sockets.
facts.evidence: source line 282: "인터커넥트 NIC 2장을 서로 다른 소켓에 연결된 슬롯으로 옮기고, 본딩을 Active-Active로 바꿔 두 포트를 동시에 쓰는 겁니다"

facts.claim: Result: the 0.1 s+ commit waits largely went away, and CPU usage dropped.
facts.evidence: source line 282: "0.1초 이상의 커밋 대기는 대부분 개선됐고"; source line 282: "36.6%에서 17.4%로"

question: https://tech.socar.kr/fe/2026/06/24/spa-cache-fallback-strategy-with-s3-cloudfront 글의 핵심을 요약해 주세요. 어떤 문제가 계기였고, 캐시와 fallback을 어떻게 나누었으며, 인프라 설정으로 해결되지 않는 부분은 어떻게 보완했나요?

facts.claim: The trigger: after a deployment, webviews still running the old SPA failed to load its old hashed chunks (chunk load errors).
facts.evidence: source line 3: "chunk load error를 계기로, 캐시 정책과 fallback 전략을 어떻게 분리했는지 정리합니다"; source line 5: "문제는 새 프론트 배포 이후 이미 열려 있던 웹뷰에서 route 이동을 할 때 발생했습니다."

facts.claim: index.html and hashed assets must have separate cache policies.
facts.evidence: source line 19: "과 hashed asset은 서로 다른 cache 정책을 가져야 한다."

facts.claim: The SPA fallback was limited to route requests, so asset requests are no longer answered with index.html; it is done with a CloudFront Function rewrite instead of the Custom Error Response.
facts.evidence: source line 21: "SPA fallback은 route 요청만 처리해야 하고, asset 요청까지 삼키면 안 된다."; source line 138: "CloudFront Function으로 route-only rewrite 적용"

facts.claim: Because infrastructure settings cannot fully prevent dynamic-import failures in already-open old SPAs, the frontend adds a reload-once defense.
facts.evidence: source line 23: "인프라 설정만으로 이미 열린 구버전 SPA의 dynamic import 실패를 완전히 없애기는 어렵다."; source line 24: "남는 런타임 문제는 프론트에서 reload-once 방어로 보완해야 한다."
